title: Ang 1000–1019: Guru Arjan and ashtpadis
tomorrow: should a hymn be read in Gurmukhi, or in words everyone gets?

cards: Two people awake at two in the morning, both staring at the ceiling. One got three job offers and can't choose; every option feels like losing the other two. The other is doing the math on rent again.
Opposite problems, same ceiling. Guru Arjan saw both of them.

Near the end of these pages, on ang 1019, he writes a line that sounds like a riddle: the house with plenty is full of worry, and the house with little wanders around searching. So who, exactly, gets to sleep?

teach.b: First, where we are. These pages of Maru carry more of Guru Arjan's hymns, the fifth Guru, and ashtpadis, longer hymns built in eight-stanza runs.
Then, on ang 1019, a set of Guru Arjan's hymns headed Anjulian, a word tied to cupped hands, the way you'd hold out your palms to receive something. And that's where the riddle sits.
In paraphrase: in the house where there is much, there is worry; in the house where there is little, a person wanders, searching.
The one who is free of both conditions is the one found at ease. Here's the twist. The Guru doesn't say get rich, and he doesn't say get poor.
He doesn't pick a side at all. Both houses lose sleep, because in both, the amount is in charge. Plenty has to be guarded.
Little has to be chased. The ease belongs to the one who isn't ruled by either, who holds out cupped hands and takes what comes. That takes nerve.
It's easier to believe one more raise would fix it, or that nothing could.
So Maru keeps doing what Maru does: it asks for courage, this time the courage to stop letting the number run the night. More courage.

how: Guru Arjan's Maru hymns, ashtpadis and the Anjulian are sung in kirtan in raga Maru and read in order in a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib.

games.q: a friend finally gets the big raise she wanted, and now she can't sleep for worrying about losing it. what would the Anjulian line say is happening?
o: the amount is still in charge; plenty just has to be guarded.
the raise wasn't big enough yet to make her secure.
money is the problem; she'd sleep fine with less.
games.why: Guru Arjan names both houses: plenty worries, little wanders. ease belongs to whoever isn't ruled by either.

practice: Rest your hands open in your lap, palms up, like cupped hands waiting. On your fingers, slowly count things you already have that are enough for today: a meal, a bed, one person who'd pick up the phone.
When you run out of fingers, just keep the palms open and breathe.
